_how_to_use: This is the delegation you SEND, not a description of one. Copy this object, replace the five
<...> placeholders in `task`, `context`, `binding`, `resources` and `timeframe`, and send it unchanged.
Do NOT compose a delegation from memory and do NOT paraphrase `findings_contract` -- the
recorded failure mode across four measured runs is reconstruction: a free-form `criteria`
string went out, `findings_contract:` did not, and the gatherer returned exactly the columns
the payload named and nothing else. Copying is the whole mechanism.
Every key below except the five placeholders is already final. Deleting, shortening or
re-wording `findings_contract` is the defect, including for a question you judged small.
`binding` is REQUIRED and is not optional for a question that looks Bedrock-shaped: a gatherer
told nothing about hosting defaults to AWS/Bedrock and returns a ledger describing a system that
is not the one failing. If the binding is not yet established, send `UNDETERMINED` and ask only
for the facts that would establish it -- never for a metric ledger.
If the delegation tool takes a single string rather than fields, serialise this object and
send it verbatim as that string, with the literal label `findings_contract:` intact.
task: <one sentence: the signal to establish and for which region/model>
context: <what the user asked, in their words, plus what is already known>
binding: <one of: bedrock | sagemaker | agentcore | self-hosted-alb | self-hosted-lambda | third-party | UNDETERMINED -- see references/hosting-bindings.md. Name the three bound slot metric names alongside it.>
resources: <account alias / region / model ids / log group, account id MASKED as <account>>

findings_contract.output_shape: Return findings ONLY as this table, one row per signal, with no prose summary.
findings_contract.table_header: | check-id | Severity | Observed value | Window | Source API | Remediation owner | AWS doc |
findings_contract.row_count_line: State your row count explicitly as `rows: <M>` on the line immediately above the table, so the count can be reconciled on the return leg.

check_ids_in_play._how_to_fill: Send the families the dispatched stage actually owns, not this whole map. Each family's severities come from that skill's own catalogue, never from your judgement.
check_ids_in_play.LLM-INV-003: ResourceNotFoundException -- model id/alias does not resolve in this region
check_ids_in_play.LLM-INV-004: AccessDeniedException -- caller not entitled to the model
check_ids_in_play.LLM-INV-005: ModelNotReadyException (HTTP 429, retried by the SDK) -- provider-side
check_ids_in_play.LLM-INV-007: ThrottlingException -- demand vs quota, backoff present or not; ServiceUnavailableException / InternalServerException -- service-side transient, retry/backoff/failover
check_ids_in_play.LLM-INV-011: ValidationException -- malformed request from the caller
check_ids_in_play._other_families: Where the dispatch is for stage depth rather than the model call, it goes to that track's skill only when that skill is available (see references/related-skills.md); that skill then reports its own family (LLM-AGT, LLM-GRD, LLM-KB, LLM-EVAL, LLM-SM, LLM-SM-SERVE, LLM-SM-BATCH and the other LLM-SM-* families) with its own severities. Without that skill, report the fallback check with no check-id.

findings_contract.observed_value_rule: `Observed value` MUST BEGIN with exactly one of the three literal tokens `measured <value>` / `no-datapoints` / `not-queried`. Never a bare number, never `zero`, `none`, `healthy`, `clean`, `no errors`, never a silent omission. There is no fourth token.
findings_contract.source_api_rule: `Source API` names the read-only call that produced the value — `cloudwatch:GetMetricData`, `cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics`, `logs:StartQuery`, `health:DescribeEvents`, `cloudtrail:LookupEvents`, `bedrock:GetFoundationModel`. A value with no API beside it is not a finding.
findings_contract.remediation_owner_rule: `Remediation owner` is the track that owns the fix, named exactly from references/related-skills.md: `bedrock-configuration` (access, entitlement, model lifecycle, wrong model ID, inference profiles), `retrieval` (knowledge base ingestion and retrieval), `caller-identities` (which IAM users and long-lived keys may call the model), `guardrails` (guardrail filter and policy behaviour), `capacity-and-quota` (quota posture, Provisioned Throughput, spend), `agent-runtime` (AgentCore or Bedrock Agents runtime, gateways, aliases), `output-quality` (output quality, truncation, finish reasons, eval gating), `sagemaker-serving` (SageMaker endpoint sizing, scaling and serving), `caller` (the caller's own request shape), `host-investigation` (compute, networking or a non-LLM component, including a self-hosted model's instances and containers). Never invent an owner and never leave the cell empty.
findings_contract.aws_doc_rule: `AWS doc` MUST be a `https://docs.aws.amazon.com/...` URL. A row without one is not a finding — omitting the citation costs you the row, not the citation.
findings_contract.error_code_enumeration: Enumerate the DISTINCT `errorCode`s with a count each, ONE ROW PER (errorCode x calling principal). A 4xx/5xx class label never stands in for the codes, and two roles failing the same way are two rows — a one-principal answer to an N-principal fault leaves N-1 callers broken. Name the principal inside the `Observed value` cell after the token, e.g. `measured 15 AccessDenied by role <role-name>`. Reconcile the per-code counts against the BOUND metric total (CLIENT_ERRORS + SERVER_ERRORS + THROTTLES; a ThrottlingException is counted in THROTTLES) over the same window and, if they do not sum, show both numbers and name the gap.
findings_contract.unaccounted_remainder: If the per-code counts do NOT sum to the metric total, RESOLVE the remainder rather than labelling or ignoring it: call `cloudtrail:LookupEvents` with AttributeKey=EventSource, AttributeValue=<bound service>.amazonaws.com (bedrock.amazonaws.com for the bedrock binding, sagemaker.amazonaws.com for sagemaker; a self-hosted binding has no control-plane event for a data-plane call, so the remainder stays not-queried unless the application logged it) over the window and read the codes AND the principals off those events. Pre-flight rejects — an unresolvable model id, a denied caller — never reach the invocation log and carry NO ModelId dimension, so the metric counts them and the log does not: that gap IS the remainder. Query by EventSource and read eventName off the results: InvokeModel and Converse are CloudTrail management events, logged by default, and an EventName=InvokeModel lookup misses every Converse call. Count only eventType AwsApiCall (streaming calls also write an AwsServiceEvent stream-completion event). NEVER assign a code to the remainder by inference: a bad model id on `Converse` returns `ValidationException` and a denied caller returns `AccessDenied`, so guessing `ResourceNotFoundException` because the id 'must not resolve' reports a 403 as a 404 and ships the wrong fix. If CloudTrail is unreadable, the remainder stays `not-queried` and is disclosed.
findings_contract.onset_window_gate: Before any claim about timing — `chronic`, `newly triggered`, `steady`, `pre-existing`, `no correlated change` — check ONE value: is the FIRST bucket of your window already non-zero? If yes, the onset is OUTSIDE your window, you have not seen it, and the only supportable statement is `non-zero throughout the window examined; onset not covered`. Widen the window until a zero/baseline bucket appears before ruling on timing. Every bucket being non-zero is what a window opened after onset looks like, not evidence that the fault is old.
findings_contract.both_metric_reads: Before reporting that errors are ruled out, query ALL THREE bound slots -- CLIENT_ERRORS, SERVER_ERRORS AND THROTTLES -- over the window and give each its own row. On the bedrock binding a throttled request is counted only in InvocationThrottles, never in InvocationClientErrors or InvocationServerErrors. A log scan alone does not support it: invocation logs do not capture pre-flight rejects, so `filter ispresent(errorCode) -> 0 records` is a fact about the log, not about the error count. On self-hosted-lambda the platform metric cannot split the two; say so in both rows rather than reporting one as zero.
findings_contract.negative_claims: Never write an unqualified `zero/no <signal>`. A negative belongs in a table row with its token, its window and its source API, or it is `not-queried`.
findings_contract.read_only: Read-only APIs only. `bedrock:ApplyGuardrail` is never called — it is billable and is not a collection call.
findings_contract.account_id: Never echo a raw AWS account id. Mask the account segment of any ARN as `<account>`.
findings_contract.gaps: Name every gap: what you could not read, and why. A denied or absent signal is recorded, never inferred away.
findings_contract.inline_identifier_rule: In ADDITION to the table, and WITHOUT removing or shortening it, write one sentence per finding under the heading `Findings in prose` placed ABOVE the table, in which the check-id, its severity and its doc URL appear INSIDE the sentence. Example: `InvocationClientErrors measured 476 over 2026-10-26T09:57Z-24h via cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics, which is LLM-INV-011 (HIGH) - https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/troubleshooting-api-error-codes.html`. Never a sentence without its id and its URL. Reason, stated so it is not optimised away: the agent that writes the final user-facing answer rewrites your report into prose and has been measured dropping every identifier that exists only inside a table cell, on every run across six iterations. An identifier inside the sentence survives that rewrite; an identifier in a cell does not. Both forms ship.
findings_contract.verdict_line: Do NOT end your report with a TRIAGE: line. That line is the dispatching skill's to write. End with your last findings row.
findings_contract.verdict_token_set_is_closed: If you are asked for a locus despite `no_conclusion_rule`, the token sets are closed and have no further members: locus is one of PROVIDER, INFRASTRUCTURE, APPLICATION, UNDETERMINED; transience is one of TRANSIENT, PERSISTENT, UNKNOWN. `no <signal> detected`, `NO THROTTLING DETECTED`, `HEALTHY` and `NOT APPLICABLE` are OBSERVATIONS, not tokens: put them in the clause after the dash. PROVIDER is unreachable on a self-hosted binding -- the customer is the provider there, so the serving layer is INFRASTRUCTURE. Do not widen either list and do not offer an extra option.
findings_contract.binding_rule: Every metric name you read MUST come from the binding named in `binding`. Reading AWS/Bedrock on a self-hosted or sagemaker binding produces a ledger of no-datapoints and a confident statement about the wrong system. If `binding` is UNDETERMINED, return ONLY the facts that would establish it -- which service serves the failing call -- and no metric ledger at all.
findings_contract.slot_names_rule: Report each of the three slots under its ABSTRACT name (CLIENT_ERRORS, SERVER_ERRORS, THROTTLES) with the bound metric name in the Source API cell. A slot the binding cannot separate carries its three-state token followed by `not-separable` and what it is folded into -- never a fourth token and never a silent omission.
findings_contract.no_conclusion_rule: You return ROWS. You do not return a locus, a TRIAGE: line, a root cause, a recommendation ranked by impact, or an operator-facing narrative. The dispatching skill assembles the locus; the host investigation rules root cause. A conclusion in your reply is something that must be re-attributed rather than forwarded, which costs the dispatch its value.
findings_contract.boundary_rule: Where the request path leaves AWS visibility, return it as its own row: the stage that is beyond visibility, which of the three slots therefore carry no AWS signal, and who holds the missing evidence (provider status page, provider support, the customer's own application telemetry). An undisclosed boundary reads as a healthy signal.

criteria: <task-specific detail ONLY — never a substitute for findings_contract, which is sent above it unchanged>
